_note: Camera's numbers for the swing that a reading can move (docs/camera/swing-view.md). A flash read or a tester can lower peakRate with no code change (Accessibility, docs/accessibility/swing-motion.md, ruling 3). The view's only: the sim never reads this.
_splitShare: against a CPU, the player's pane takes this share of the split, 0.5 to 1; 0 is even. Orb's first play asked for about 0.7 (docs/camera/split-unequal.md); both of Orb's 9 November builds played 0.7, and it is main's since A-CAMERA-01
_pieces: the camera Orb played on 9 November (A-CAMERA-01), each on at a plain start: the swing with the turning world (docs/camera/swing-view.md), the peak launch shot, the launch director (docs/camera/launch-director.md), the close brawl, the readable size, the follow-through and the flight reveal. Until A-CAMERA-01 they rode on the tile-ground start word. swingView and peakLaunch also need the globe ground drawn (render/core/main.gd): the peak shot's widest view needs the globe, so on the flat ground they stay off whatever this says
_flatMode: a flat send's shot (docs/camera/launch-director.md): wide (Orb's builds), hold, or empty for none; a start word flat=wide or flat=hold still chooses it for a comparison
_peakRate: the peak launch's zoom, e-folds a second at most. 3 is Research's: 93% of the descent in frame, against 34% at 1. A slower number loses the falling fighter out of the frame
